title: Emerging variants of SARS-CoV-2 NSP10 highlight strong functional conservation of its binding to two non-structural proteins, NSP14 and NSP16
authors: Wang H; Rizvi SRA; Dong D; Lou J; Wang Q; Sopipong W; Su Y; Najar F; Agarwal PK; Kozielski F; Haider S
one_liner_zh: 该文研究SARS-CoV-2 NSP10变异对其与NSP14/NSP16蛋白结合的影响，虽涉及蛋白-蛋白互作和增强采样模拟，但对象非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题TF-DNA结合研究无关。
abstract:
The coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 protects its RNA from being recognized by host immune responses by methylation of its 5’ end, also known as capping. This process is carried out by two enzymes, non-structural protein 16 (NSP16) containing 2’-O-methyltransferase and NSP14 through its N7 methyltransferase activity, which are essential for the replication of the viral genome as well as evading the host’s innate immunity. NSP10 acts as a crucial cofactor and stimulator of NSP14 and NSP16. To further understand the role of NSP10, we carried out a comprehensive analysis of >13 million globally collected whole-genome sequences (WGS) of SARS-CoV-2 obtained from the Global Initiative Sharing All Influenza Data (GISAID) and compared it with the reference genome Wuhan/WIV04/2019 to identify all currently known variants in NSP10. T12I, T102I, and A104V in NSP10 have been identified as the three most frequent variants and characterized using X-ray crystallography, biophysical assays and enhanced sampling simulations. In contrast to other proteins such as spike and NSP6, NSP10 is significantly less prone to mutation due to its crucial role in replication. The functional effects of the variants were examined for their impact on the binding affinity and stability of both NSP14-NSP10 and NSP16-NSP10 complexes. These results highlight the limited changes induced by variant evolution in NSP10 and reflect on the critical roles NSP10 plays during the SARS-CoV-2 life cycle. These results also indicate that there is limited capacity for the virus to overcome inhibitors targeting NSP10 via the generation of variants in inhibitor binding pockets.

Significance Statement

The SARS-CoV-2 proteins have constantly been evolving. These variants assist the virus to survive, adapt and evade the host immune responses. While the main focus has been on structural proteins like Spike, there is very limited structural and functional information on the effects of emerging mutations on other essential non-structural viral proteins. One such protein is NSP10, an essential cofactor for NSP14 and NSP16. This study demonstrates that NSP10 is more resistant to genetic variations than other SARS-CoV-2 non-structural proteins and that the presence of mutations conserve structural and dynamic changes in NSP10. The effects of naturally occurring mutations reflect the evolutionary relationship between structurally conserved essential cofactors, their function and the role they play in the survival of the virus.
abstract_zh:
冠状病毒SARS-CoV-2通过对其5'端进行甲基化（即加帽）来保护其RNA免受宿主免疫反应的识别。这一过程由两种酶执行：含有2'-O-甲基转移酶的非结构蛋白16（NSP16）和通过其N7甲基转移酶活性发挥作用的NSP14，这两种酶对病毒基因组的复制以及逃避宿主先天免疫至关重要。NSP10作为NSP14和NSP16的关键辅因子和刺激因子。为进一步理解NSP10的作用，我们对从全球共享流感数据倡议组织（GISAID）获取的超过1300万条全球收集的SARS-CoV-2全基因组序列（WGS）进行了全面分析，并与参考基因组Wuhan/WIV04/2019进行比较，以识别NSP10中所有当前已知的变异。NSP10中的T12I、T102I和A104V被确定为三种最常见的变异，并通过X射线晶体学、生物物理测定和增强采样模拟进行了表征。与刺突蛋白和NSP6等其他蛋白相比，NSP10因其在复制中的关键作用而显著不易发生突变。我们检查了这些变异对NSP14-NSP10和NSP16-NSP10复合物结合亲和力和稳定性的功能影响。这些结果突显了变异进化在NSP10中诱导的有限变化，并反映了NSP10在SARS-CoV-2生命周期中发挥的关键作用。这些结果还表明，病毒通过抑制剂结合口袋中产生变异来克服靶向NSP10的抑制剂的能力有限。

意义声明

SARS-CoV-2蛋白持续进化。这些变异帮助病毒生存、适应并逃避宿主免疫反应。虽然主要关注点集中在刺突蛋白等结构蛋白上，但对于新出现的突变对其他必需非结构病毒蛋白的影响，结构和功能信息非常有限。NSP10就是这样一种蛋白，它是NSP14和NSP16的必需辅因子。本研究证明，NSP10比其他SARS-CoV-2非结构蛋白更能抵抗遗传变异，并且突变的存在保持了NSP10的结构和动态变化。自然发生的突变效应反映了结构保守的必需辅因子、其功能及其在病毒生存中所起作用之间的进化关系。
